items.title: Nothing teases a screen-free AI device ahead of launch next month
items.excerpt: CEO Carl Pei says Nothing’s first “AI-native” device “couldn’t have been an app.”
items.rationale: On-record CEO tease of Nothing's first AI-native, screen-free device with a launch next month. The 10-19 card was only an unconfirmed report about smart glasses.

items.title: Gemini for Home now plugs into AT&T’s smart security system
items.excerpt: Google's Gemini for Home now connects to AT&T's Connected Life smart security system, bringing Gemini's AI features to the carrier's home security setup.
items.rationale: New integration: Gemini for Home now reaches a carrier home-security system, so it spreads past Google's own hardware.

items.title: Disneyland Is Training a Class of AI Robot Interns
items.excerpt: From Pixar robots to help you park your car to droids roaming Star Wars land, physical AI is popping up all over Disneyland.
items.rationale: Physical AI in public: Disneyland is putting AI robots to work with guests, from parking helpers to droids. A clear consumer-facing example of embodied AI.

items.title: Apple Watch learned new hand gestures in just a minute. It’s the most exciting wearable research I’ve seen in years.
items.excerpt: Researchers have developed a system called TransfHAR that uses the motion sensors inside the Apple Watch, the accelerometer and the gyroscope, to learn and identify activities based on the movement of your hands and wrist.
items.rationale: New research (TransfHAR) that teaches the Apple Watch a custom hand gesture from the stock motion sensors in about a minute. Points toward user-defined gesture input on wearables.

items.title: This treadmill owner used Claude to escape a subscription trap, and it's glorious
items.excerpt: NordicTrack wanted another subscription. One owner had other plans, and Claude helped turn those plans into a clever treadmill makeover.
items.rationale: A NordicTrack owner used Claude to break free of the iFit subscription, a hands-on example of AI-assisted hardware modding by consumers.

https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i.new_action: Official announcement: Carl Pei publicly teased Nothing's first 'AI-native', screen-free device and set the launch for next month. The 10-19 card was an unconfirmed report about two pairs of smart glasses.
